restatements.text: Declares that the state has exclusive authority over minimum wage regulation and voids all city ordinances that set a minimum wage.

findings.direction: shifts authority from local governments to the state
findings.quote: The state occupies the whole field of minimum wage regulation. Any city ordinance setting a minimum wage is void.
findings.mechanism: Preempts cities from regulating minimum wages, centralizing this authority entirely at the state level.

findings.quote: Any city ordinance setting a minimum wage is void.
findings.mechanism: Eliminates existing city minimum wage ordinances and prevents future ones, removing workers' ability to receive locally mandated minimum pay that exceeds the state standard.

findings.quote: The state occupies the whole field of minimum wage regulation. Any city ordinance setting a minimum wage is void.
findings.mechanism: Standardizes minimum wage requirements statewide, relieving businesses from complying with a patchwork of local regulations and preventing cities from imposing higher mandated wage costs.

analysis.answer: Current law permits cities to set minimum wages higher than the state minimum. The measure changes this by asserting exclusive state control over minimum wage laws and voiding any existing city minimum wage ordinances.

Businesses operating in cities with local minimum wage laws benefit from standardized and potentially lower minimum wage mandates. Workers in those cities who rely on the higher local minimum wage bear the cost of lower mandated pay.

Businesses operating across multiple cities will face a single statewide minimum wage, simplifying payroll and compliance. Employers in cities with previously higher minimum wages may adjust their hiring, expansion, or pricing practices. Workers in high-cost cities may experience decreased purchasing power without localized wage minimums.

The measure addresses the compliance complexity and varied labor costs businesses face from a patchwork of local wage laws by voiding all local ordinances. Conversely, it prevents local governments from using higher wage mandates to address higher local living costs.
State lawmakers gain exclusive authority over minimum wage policy, while city councils lose the power to set local minimum wages. Employers gain protection from localized wage mandates.

The impact of eliminating higher local minimum wages on jobs and investment is disputed. Some research suggests that lowering mandated wage floors boosts local hiring and business investment by reducing labor costs, while other research finds that higher local minimum wages do not significantly reduce employment and can increase local economic activity through higher worker spending.

items.text: Standardized minimum wage rules that relieve businesses from navigating varying local regulations and prevent cities from imposing higher wage costs.
The ability of workers to benefit from higher minimum wages mandated by city ordinances.
Shifts the authority to set minimum wages entirely from local governments to the state.
Workers' ability to be paid higher minimum wages as required by their local city ordinances.
A uniform statewide minimum wage that simplifies compliance and caps mandated wage costs for businesses by eliminating higher local requirements.
